newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy condemns "worrying" violence in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Italy condemns "worrying" violence in Serbia.

text.p: Italy on Monday condemned clashes between Serbian police and protesters and urged hardline President Slobodan Milosevic to reinstate annulled election victories by the opposition coalition.

Diplomatic sources said Italy, which recently invited the leaders of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition to Rome for talks with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, was "watching with great concern recent developments of the crisis in Serbia".

They said Rome "condemns any act of violence that risks sparking a deterioration of the situation and reaffirms...that the situation can only be unblocked by the Belgrade government fully accepting the results of the November 17 elections".
Scores of angry youths hurled stones at Serb riot police on Monday hours after more than 100 pro-democracy protesters were injured in the bloodiest street battles in Belgrade for years.
Vesna Pesic, one of the three co-leaders of Zajedno, was clubbed in the back and thigh by police.
Demonstrators have held nearly three months of peaceful protests to demand the restoration of opposition victories in elections in 14 Serbian municipalities, including Belgrade.
The West has demanded that Milosevic abide by the conclusions of an OSCE mission which investigated the elections in Serbia and verified that the opposition had won them.
Italy last week hosted a meeting of the multinational Contact Group on former Yugoslavia which appealed to both sides to refrain from violence.
